Section on clock distribution (early-to-: Adopted a globally distributed, buffered clock tree (described with multiple levels of buffering driving a large number of clock pins using programmable/active deskew buffers at the local clock generator (LCG) level to correct for systematic skew across the chip.
alternatives_or_rejected: The paper explicitly argues against the alternative of a single global clock driver or a simple H-tree without deskew, on the grounds that at POWER4 frequencies and die size the uncompensated PVT/skew variation would exceed the available-period budget. It also contrasts against a pure grid (mesh) distribution as either insufficiently structured or as more power warranted.
rationale: The combination of structured tree distribution and deskew is presented as the way to meet aggressive cycle-time targets across large die while controlling clock power and avoiding the area/routing overhead of a full grid. Deskew corrects for the systematic that a tree alone cannot remove.
outcome: The paper reports that meets the target frequency across the die with acceptable power, enabling the synchronous design methodology used elsewhere in the chip. It specifically creditsew mechanism with removing residual skew after the tree.
